# 1 Clement Chapter 47 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 47

---

## Council Notes

**On "blessed Paul the Apostle" (v.1):** EMET: "blessed Paul the Apostle." LOGOS: "blessed Apostle Paul." PNEUMA: "blessed Apostle Paul." The Greek order is *Paulou tou apostolou* — name first, then title. EMET preserved. This is significant: Clement names Paul before attributing apostolic authority, suggesting familiarity.

**On "in the beginning of the gospel" (v.2):** EMET/LOGOS: "at the beginning of the gospel." PNEUMA: "at the beginning of his message." The Greek *ep' archēs tou euangeliou* is a recognizable Pauline phrase (cf. Phil 4:15). "At the beginning of the gospel" (LOGOS) is retained as honoring the technical sense.

**On "attested by God" (v.4):** All agents agree. The Greek *memarturēmenous* (testified/witnessed) refers to divine commendation of the apostles.

**On "those who differ from us" / "those outside our number" (v.7):** EMET: "those who differ from us." LOGOS: "those outside our number." PNEUMA: "those outside our fellowship." The Greek *tois heteroklinesi* means "those who lean otherwise / dissidents." This appears to refer to non-Christians or potentially pagans who observe the church's behavior. "Those outside our fellowship" (PNEUMA) is most readable; "those who differ from us" (EMET) preserves the Greek shade of meaning. EMET retained.

**Historical note (v.3):** This is a direct citation of the situation described in 1 Corinthians 1:12 and 3:4-5. Clement appeals to the Corinthians' own scripture to shame them. The factionalism of c.50s CE Corinth has recurred c.96 CE Corinth.

---

**47:1** Take up the epistle of the blessed Paul the Apostle.

**47:2** What did he first write to you at the beginning of the gospel?

**47:3** In truth he wrote to you with spiritual insight concerning himself and Cephas and Apollos, because even then you had formed factions.

**47:4** Yet that partisanship brought less sin upon you — for you were making yourselves partisans of apostles attested by God, and of a man approved by them.

**47:5** But now consider who it is that has led you astray and diminished the honor of your celebrated brotherly affection.

**47:6** It is shameful, beloved, wholly shameful and unworthy of your manner of life in Christ, that on account of one or two persons the very steadfast and ancient church of the Corinthians is reported to be in revolt against its presbyters.

**47:7** And this report has come not only to us, but also to those who differ from us — so that blasphemies are heaped upon the name of the Lord because of your foolishness, and peril is brought upon yourselves as well.

---

*— SOPHIA*
